pass_a_gloss: And if to someone such a thing appears difficult, he did not thirst toward God the strong the living, nor did he yearn toward God in the way the hind yearns toward the springs of the waters, nor did he say: when then will I arrive and be seen to the face of God? nor did he reckon in himself the things which, reckoning them through, the prophet, there being said to him the 'where is your God' each day, poured out upon himself his soul, striking at it while still according to weakness it was becoming very grieved and being stirred up together, and saying: that I will go through in a place of a marvellous tent as far as the house of God, in a voice of exultation and of confession, of a sound feasting.
pass_b_english: If anyone finds such a thing hard, he has not “thirsted for God, the mighty, the living” (Psalm 42:2); he has not longed for God “as the deer longs for the springs of water” (Psalm 42:1); nor has he said, “When then shall I come and appear before the face of God?” (Psalm 42:2). Nor has he pondered within himself what the prophet pondered when, as “Where is your God?” was said to him “every day” (Psalm 42:3), he poured out “his soul” upon himself, rebuking his soul when, through weakness, it was still growing sorrowful and troubled, and saying: “For I will pass through into the place of the wonderful tent, as far as the house of God, with a voice of rejoicing and thanksgiving, the sound of one keeping festival” (Psalm 42:4).

Read ἐδίψησε (OCR ἐδίunse), ἔλαφος, τοῦ θεοῦ, ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ θεός σου (OCR ποῖ ... 6), ἔτι κατ᾽ ἀσθένειαν περιλύπῳ γινομένῃ (PTA confirms ἔτι ... περιλύπῳ), ὅτι διελεύσομαι (OCR οὔτε; PTA confirms ὅτι), ἀγαλλιάσεως καὶ (OCR 'a ἰγαλλιάσεως κεὼ').
Rendered “For I will pass through”: ὅτι introduces the quoted words and also carries the Psalm's causal sense.
